messages:
maria_cs: Quick — drafted a customer-facing 1-pager runbook for Acadia (renewal next month). Goal: make demos feel instant, reduce renewal risk by ensuring warm pools/prefill, graceful streaming fallback, and a tight feedback capture loop. PTAL and flag gaps.

aj_dev: Can you paste the checklist here? short bullets so AE can read before the call.

maria_cs: Sure — paste below. This is intentionally terse for customer-facing use: 

- Purpose: keep demo latency predictable and show deterministic quality during renewal window.
- Owner: CS + Eng enablement (maria_cs / aj_dev).
- Pre-demo prep (48h -> 1h):
  • 48h: request warm pool reservation (size based on 95th pct usage).
  • 6h: run a prefill job against the tenant to populate common prefixes.
  • 1h: dry-run short end-to-end demo with streaming enabled.
- Live settings to recommend to customer (API-level):
  • Prefill TTL: 3600s for demo tenants.
  • Batch hints: target_batch=8, max_latency=50ms.
  • Streaming: enabled with fallback to non-stream after 200ms no-chunk.
- Observability: confirm token-level latency and first-byte in dashboard; capture last-5 prompt traces.
- Feedback capture: short 3-question survey after demo + optional sample of 2 transcripts for quality triage.
- Escalation: if 95th latency > 200ms during demo, switch to low-cost model variant and notify CS oncall.

aj_dev: Pasting the prefill command we use in infra playbooks so ops can copy it: 
```bash
# prefill warm pool for tenant 'acadia'
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/prefill" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"tenant":"acadia","prompt":"demo-warmup","pool_size":12,"ttl_sec":3600}'
```

maria_cs: also adding a tiny batch config snippet customers can drop into their integration: 
```json
{"batch_size":8, "max_latency_ms":50, "enable_stream":true, "stream_fallback_ms":200}
```

kevin_pm: Love it. A couple asks for the one-pager: add two quick success metrics we can cite in renewal convo (FB latency < 150ms, steady-state token cost delta < 8%). Also add next steps: 3-day check-in after demo to collect survey.

elena_support: Add a line about consent for storing transcripts (GDPR). For feedback capture we should use a short link (tiny.redwood/feedback-acadia) and include an auto-attach of 2 anonymized transcripts if they opt-in.

maria_cs: Good catches — updated the checklist and survey flow. I included an opt-in checkbox copy: 
  • "I consent to share anonymized transcripts for quality review."

aj_dev: Two practical notes for the enablement handoff: 
1) If the tenant uses custom system prompts, prefill should include the exact system prompt variant to avoid drift.
2) If warm pool fails to fill, fallback to a 'soft-warm' mode where we pre-create KV caches for top 20 prefixes.

maria_cs: Copy. Adding a short troubleshooting triage at the bottom:
- Symptom: warm pool empty on demo start -> Action: run `prefill` with pool_size 2x baseline and notify infra; enable soft-warm.
- Symptom: streaming stalls -> Action: toggle stream_fallback_ms to 150ms and restart demo session.
- Symptom: customer reports hallucination spike after prefill -> Action: rollback prefill and run eval set against model.

ops_bot: Reminder (automated): schedule reserved capacity slot with eng-infra 2024-11-18T15:00:00Z for tenant 'acadia' — respond with :thumbsup: to confirm.

kevin_pm: Can we add a one-line risk summary for the AE? "Risk: renewal sensitive to demo latency and hallucination; mitigation: warm pools + prefills + quick rollback plan."

maria_cs: Done. I'll also attach the survey template in the wiki. Final ask: can one of you run through the dry-run with me Thursday 14:00? @aj_dev @elena_support

aj_dev: I can do Thursday 14:00. :thumbsup:

elena_support: I'll join and bring consent wording for EU tenants.

maria_cs: Thanks team — I'll send the one-pager to the AE after the dry-run. Leaving here for audit: short checklist + snippets + escalation path. 👍
